source: distilled from the reference implementation and an inventory of its 206 raw concepts

concepts.name: invariant
concepts.definition: The abstract behavioral requirement for a feature, system, or mechanism. No matter what additions or removals, the invariant must be preserved across implementations. If the invariant is removed or violated, this must be immediately revealed and evaluated by an agent and their human operator, or Coherence has failed as a system.

rejected.alternative: invariant includes its enforcement (the reference gate/guarantee bundle)
rejected.because: the invariant is abstract; it must survive any implementation, so enforcement points at it rather than being part of it

rejected.alternative: agent may retire an invariant with only a recorded decision
rejected.because: removing a vertebra alters the shape and integrity of the system; a human must acknowledge
agents decompose requirements into invariants freely during planning; announcement suffices, and growth in detail protects load-bearing members

rejected.alternative: revelation at verify or at read time as the primary channel
rejected.because: the primary moment is the edit inside the agent session; later moments are fallbacks when the economics are impractical

rejected.alternative: a facility concept above components that invariants belong to
rejected.because: the folder tree already expresses containment; the nearest common ancestor folder is the home of a relationship invariant

rejected.alternative: a flat project-level set of invariants
rejected.because: coupling to the protected resource is what keeps the invariant legible next to the code it constrains

revelation.when: At the moment of the edit, inside the agent's session. If the economics of that are not practical, at the next nearest practical moment (the fallback ladder is an implementation question, not part of the concept).
revelation.who: The editing agent first. A violation that stands must be a conscious decision, made as the result of a refactor, move, or retirement of the larger class of facility the invariant protects.
revelation.owner_words: if the invariant has been violated, this must be a conscious decision, as the result of a refactor, move or retirement of the larger class of facility the invariant is protecting. if the economics of this are not practical, then the alarm should come at the next nearest, practical moment.

retirement.rule: Any retired invariant must be acknowledged by the human operator. The agent may propose retirement with a recorded decision; the invariant stays in force, and alarming, until a person acknowledges.
retirement.reference_verbs: decide (with the rejected alternative being preservation) plus escalate and acknowledge; the reference has the verbs but no link from a decision to the invariant it retires.
retirement.owner_words: the human should absolutely acknowledge any retired invariant.
retirement.reliance_listing: At retirement the tool lists every component that relies on the invariant, computed from imports of its chokepoint; the human acknowledges with that list in view.

authoring.rule: Asymmetric. An agent may propose new invariants as part of planning new work, decomposing requirements freely, and must announce each declaration. Only removal requires human acknowledgement.
authoring.origin: Invariants fall out of requirements. A requirement like "this is a session-secured resource that can only be accessed by a user with permissions" implicitly contains invariant instances.
authoring.growth: Growing more detailed is good. Most projects need a structure closer to an automobile than an octopus; detailed invariants make sure load-bearing members are not opaquely weakened to serve feature work or refactors.
authoring.owner_words: an agent can propose new invariants as a process of planning new work ... the agent may decompose this stuff freely, but should also announce such invariant declaration.

detail.lifecycle: requirement (declared, not yet enforced) -> invariant (requirement satisfied by detection) -> structural defect (invariant whose satisfaction has been removed)

home.rule: An invariant couples as closely as possible to the resource whose behavior it protects. If it must describe two components in relationship, it belongs in the super folder containing both. The spec tree is the only home; no facility concept.
home.owner_words: invariants couple as closely as possible to the resource whose behavior they protect. if an invariant must be able to describe two components in relationship, then the invariant belongs in the super folder containing both components. no new concept needed

security_marker.rule: Not a boolean. An expressive, machine-readable marker on the invariant, starting with a crossing: "crossing A -> B" where A and B are trust levels from a short list the entry spec declares. Tracing the security spine is a query over crossings; more expressive forms may be added later.
security_marker.trust_levels: Declared once in the entry spec as a short list with one-line meanings (Mnemion example: owner-trusted, storage, served-untrusted, public-egress, agent-mcp, federated). Spec, not config. They are trust levels of data or callers, never places in the code.
security_marker.owner_words: no boolean, make the marker more expressive, starting with crossing

because.rule: Each invariant carries its own because: why it exists, what it protects against. Replaces the ## why section. Rationale that restates the mechanism belongs nowhere.

provenance.metaphor: Invariants are the spine of the system. Removing any vertebra may have significant consequences because it alters the fundamental shape of the system and its integrity. Most projects need a structure closer to an automobile than an octopus.
provenance.reference_note: In the reference the authored form is one bullet under ## invariants; enforcement (boundary claim: chokepoint + oracle + crossing) and refutation history are separate records that the render layers fold back in under different names.
working_readings: A surviving violation is a recorded decision with the rejected alternative being preservation.
Removing an invariant from the spec without an acknowledged retirement is itself a violation and is revealed the same way.
An invariant is a requirement satisfied by detection. Enforcement is a separate concept that points at it and is what makes a requirement an invariant.

concepts.name: requirement
concepts.definition: The invariant state before enforcement. A declared behavioral requirement that nothing yet detects the violation of. Falls out of planning; an agent may declare one freely and must announce it. A requirement becomes an invariant only after enforcement is witnessed AND every applicable decomposition-checklist shape has been declared or dismissed.

concepts.name: structural defect
concepts.definition: An invariant whose satisfaction has been removed. The enforcement that made the requirement an invariant no longer detects. Revealed at the edit in the agent session; stands until a human acknowledges a retirement or the enforcement is restored.

rejected.because: a former name for this concept in the reference implementation; refused so it cannot return as a second spelling

concepts.name: enforcement
concepts.definition: The category of things that satisfy a requirement by detection, turning it into an invariant. Two options: a chokepoint (ideal) or a totality oracle (the compromise). Enforcement counts as detection only once its refutation has been witnessed; chokepoints refute themselves through symbol resolution, totality oracles must be witnessed.

detail.cardinality: One invariant may have several enforcements, grouped under it as evidence paths (reference decision d-6642c854). One enforcement serves one invariant; if a chokepoint protects two requirements, they are two invariants naming the same chokepoint.

provenance.reference_note: In the reference a boundary claim carries BOTH a chokepoint and an oracle; here they are alternatives under one category.
working_readings: Cardinality follows the reference decision d-6642c854: one invariant may have several enforcements as evidence paths, grouped under the one invariant rather than rendered as several. Adopted unless the owner objects.

concepts.name: chokepoint
concepts.definition: A structural fact: the one site through which every reference to a protected thing passes. A chokepoint claim names two things, the protected thing (a symbol or a module, so the concept generalizes across kinds of systems) and the chokepoint symbol. It holds while every resolved reference to the protected thing is inside the chokepoint; the moment a second referencing site exists, it is no longer a chokepoint, and that edit is the moment to reveal it. The chokepoint itself may have any number of callers.

rejected.alternative: the chokepoint symbol itself has one and only one caller
rejected.because: the chokepoint is what many paths cross; the single-caller constraint belongs to the protected thing behind it

rejected.alternative: existence of the chokepoint symbol in the code graph is sufficient (the reference behavior)
rejected.because: existence detects nothing; a bypass path is invisible to it, so under the lifecycle it is a requirement, not an invariant

detail.detection: AST and symbol resolution, not a test run. Cheap enough to run at the edit.
detail.site_forms: Two reference sites carry a form the language gives them, and the form is read before the range (owner's ruling d-7abd1ba8, 2026-09-18). A plain import specifier, type-only and namespace imports included, is inside when it sits in the chokepoint's own module: that one location is how the chokepoint reaches the protected thing, not a place the thing is used. The same import anywhere else is a bypass. An export-from specifier or a wildcard re-export is a bypass wherever it stands, the chokepoint's own module included, because it widens the thing's reach with no call at all. Python's equivalents: from x import y or import x at the top of the chokepoint's module is inside; an import whose name the module's __all__ lists is a re-export, and so is a bare from x import *. Every other site is classified by range.

protected_thing.note: module privacy is the natural unit when several members of one module legitimately touch the protected state

properties.exempt reference: A reference to the protected thing from inside the folder a chokepoint bullet's from: line exempts (from: outside the component, or from: outside <folder>; the config's chokepointFrom when the bullet is silent; from: anywhere, the default, exempts nothing). It is classed exempt and reported with the from: value that governed and who said it, never a bypass and never dropped, so a module boundary lets the module use its own internals while a narrow invariant counts every reference.

concepts.name: totality oracle
concepts.definition: The compromise enforcement, used where structural encoding of the invariant is not practical: a detector that checks the invariant holds over the whole named set it is total over. Totality is the required form of the compromise; a spot check is not enforcement. Requires a witnessed refutation before it counts as enforcement.

provenance.reference_note: The reference recently required a totality claim to name the set it is total over (commit 05f3ea5); the reference also uses "oracle" for the machine that grades tests, which this concept does not cover.

concepts.name: chokepoint grade
concepts.definition: A legible, generalizable grade for the structural quality of a chokepoint. It nudges the agent toward a better form and reflects chokepoint strength to the user.

ladder.meaning: the protected thing is not exported from the chokepoint module; the compiler enforces the choke and the AST check only confirms non-export plus single reference. Nothing outside the module can bypass. The ideal.
the protected thing is exported, but every resolved reference in the repository is inside the chokepoint. A consumer outside the repository could still bypass, so this ranks below visibility-choked.

the protected thing is reached dynamically (string-keyed access, reflection, raw SQL strings, network, subprocess, another language). No AST can count callers; a totality oracle is the required compromise and the claim must say why structure was unavailable.

detail.adapter_defined: The ladder is defined per language adapter and each rung names who enforces it. TypeScript: visibility-choked (the compiler), reference-choked (Coherence), not chokeable. Python: closure-choked (the interpreter, when the protected thing is never a module attribute), checker-choked (Pyright private-usage at error in the project configuration; an import-linter contract for a protected module), reference-choked (Coherence, at the edit and in CI), convention (nobody), not chokeable. A rung the project must configure is shown as such, never assumed.
detail.refutation_by_rung: Who enforces the rung decides what refutes it (owner's ruling rs-e93ecdd6, 2026-09-18). Where Coherence's own check is the enforcer, the refutation stages synthetic references and the check's own classification must call each one a bypass. Where the language is the enforcer, visibility-choked and closure-choked, Coherence's check can never be made to fire, because the compiler refuses every import of a thing its module does not export and the interpreter refuses every import of a name that is not a module attribute; there the adapter stages the synthetic outside reference and asks the language server for the diagnostic, and a diagnostic saying the name is not exported or not accessible is the refutation, recorded as refused by the language with its text. Demanding Coherence's own firing on those rungs would leave the strongest rungs weaker than the one below them.

provenance.reference_note: The reference has an ordinal A..U grade that is a total function of recorded signals on a gate; this replaces it with a ladder whose rungs name structural facts.

concepts.name: refutation
concepts.definition: The witnessed firing of an enforcement: the invariant was broken and the detector went red. Required. Enforcement does not count as detection, and a requirement does not become an invariant, until its refutation has been witnessed. The same hygiene as writing a test for a new feature.

rejected.alternative: graded: a refutation raises the grade, absence is tolerated
rejected.because: a detector never seen to fire is not evidence of detection; a green test that has never been red proves nothing

by_option.chokepoint: Provided transparently by the tool. The language server or equivalent symbol resolution proves that a second reference to the protected thing would be reported, so no one stages the break by hand.
by_option.totality oracle: Must be witnessed and recorded: what was broken and what was seen. Until then the oracle is a requirement, not enforcement.

provenance.reference_note: The reference records refutations as <invariant>: <what was broken> -> <what was seen> and reports coverage over them but never fails on a missing one. Here absence blocks the transition from requirement to invariant.

concepts.name: component
concepts.definition: Any folder with a spec file. A component is the aggregate of an implementation, its spec definition, and the practice file paired with that spec when it has one. Subcomponents are declared by specs in child folders; folders without a spec are transparent. A super folder becomes a component when a relationship invariant about its children needs a home there.

rejected.because: the spec is what declares the unit; a folder without one is transparent
the spec file in place is the declaration; config would be a second spelling

concepts.name: reliance
concepts.definition: A computed fact, never declared: the components whose code references a chokepoint (or the protected thing behind it) rely on that invariant. Listed at retirement time so the human acknowledging a retired invariant sees who depends on it, and modeled and displayed in Scope.

rejected.alternative: declared guarantee consumer links (relies on / addresses)
rejected.because: 3 instances each; their prose is a relationship invariant, which already has a home in the super folder under the home rule; the hash ids are unreadable

rejected.alternative: declared handoffs as labeled import edges for the map
rejected.because: the reliance listing computed from imports is the map; an authored label with no verification weight is a second spelling

properties.targets: Both references to the chokepoint and references to its protected thing contribute to reliance. Their roles remain visible, so a protected bypass is not mislabeled as a legal reference to the door.
properties.incomplete_evidence: Legacy, unresolved, unavailable or failed reference collection remains unknown. Definition files and touched-file lists alone do not establish reliance.

concepts.name: decomposition checklist
concepts.definition: A prosthetic for systematic thinking that fires when an agent declares a requirement. The tool asks two closed questions: what set is this total over (the totality grammar), and, for the kind of thing being protected, which of the known invariant shapes apply. Each applicable shape must be declared as an invariant or dismissed with a reason before the requirement can become an invariant. Dismissals are recorded so a considered refusal never looks like an unexamined gap.

rejected.alternative: taxonomy (roles, facets, obligations, caller-assessed classification records)
rejected.because: systematicity about what exists rather than what must hold; a second ontology with its own records, ids, revisions, and staleness that competed with the spine for maintenance

rejected.alternative: guarantee catalog as linked machinery with hash ids and assessments
rejected.because: the sentences are good, the machinery around them is strata; zero unchanged fits in the reference assay
the goal of forcing ontology is legitimate; only the moment and the output form were wrong

detail.content: The 36 guarantee-catalog sentences from the reference, re-keyed by what the requirement protects rather than by the role a file plays. Prose shapes only: no ids, no assessments, no links, no activation rules.

provenance.reference_note: The reference forced ontology at code-classification time (taxonomy roles activating obligations), producing 79 obligations and 3 links for one component and an unresolved vocabulary escalation; its portability assay found zero unchanged fits across 112 attempts.
provenance.purpose: Models struggle to behave with systematicity; given one requirement they write one invariant where a systematic thinker writes five. The checklist forces enumeration at the moment the agent has a specific subject in hand, and its output is a first-class thing (an invariant or a recorded dismissal), never a parallel record.

concepts.name: reference
concepts.definition: A resolved use of one symbol by another site, as the language server reports it. The only dependency fact the system reasons over. Chokepoint detection, the reliance listing, and any dependency picture are computed from references; a module-level import map is at most a view over them.

rejected.alternative: imports as a claim form or as the dependency graph
rejected.because: an import says a module mentions a module, not which symbol or whether it is the protected one; low information, and references subsume it once a language server is the instrument

properties.protected_reference: A reference whose target is the protected thing. Its inside, test or bypass classification is used for the invariant verdict.
properties.chokepoint_reference: An external static reference whose target is the chokepoint. It may be an import, re-export, type use, value use or invocation; it does not assert runtime execution.
properties.site_evidence: Recorded sites distinguish their target and test location. A present empty list means both reference queries completed with no sites; a missing list is incomplete evidence, never proof of no reliance.

concepts.name: crossing
concepts.definition: The first form of the security marker on an invariant: crossing A -> B names the trust levels on either side of the invariant's chokepoint. Lets "every chokepoint where agent input reaches storage" be a query. Where the chokepoint is an entrance's handler, its entering side must equal the trust level the entrance declares, and is the entrance's trust, labeled derived, when it declares none. It says which trust an invariant checks, never where that trust enters: an invariant enforced by a totality oracle alone is a control only on the entrances its entrances: line names, never on every entrance whose trust its crossing matches. Carries no topology and nothing renders from it but the spine.

rejected.because: a former name for this concept in the reference implementation; refused so it cannot return as a second spelling

provenance.reference_note: Mnemion: 12 of 16 boundary claims carry a crossing over 6 declared trust levels. Coherence itself never used the form and put the same information in 62 atlas transitions in config.

concepts.name: trust level
concepts.definition: One entry in the short list the entry spec declares for crossings and entrances: a name and a one-line meaning for a class of data or caller. A level marked (outside) comes from outside the system's control; an entrance carrying it with no control traced on its route is marked no traced control. Declared order carries no meaning. Not a place in the code and not a container of components.

rejected.alternative: zones as a topology with residence (lives in) and nesting (inside)
rejected.because: components already nest; a trust level only needs to exist so a crossing can name it

concepts.name: spec
concepts.definition: The file that makes a folder a component. Contains: a one-line intent; the invariants, each with its enforcement (chokepoint with protected thing, or totality oracle over a named set), its because, its crossing where security-relevant, and its refutation; and, in the entry spec only, the list of trust levels. One bullet grammar: every bullet is an invariant with enforcement. Its sister is the practice file, which holds the component's practices in the same bullet grammar and never exists without it.

provenance.reference_note: The reference split one invariant across four sections (invariants, works when, refutations, why) and let works-when hold claims with no invariant behind them. Here the invariant is the unit and the sections collapse into it.

concepts.name: journal
concepts.definition: Compression. The journal compresses possibly millions of subagent session tokens into a handful of durable, comprehensible outcomes. It is also a signaling system so subagents can compare notes, and a means of escalation to humans. Getting a pile of code into RAM is expensive; the journal exists to maximize the value extracted while the cache is hot. A record may cite the earlier records it rests on or is about (a citation, checked at the write and read both ways), and a decision, escalation or acknowledgement may carry words the agent attributes to a human, kept apart from its own because; that records the attribution, not proof a human wrote them.

detail.caution: Population comparisons across projects are unreliable here: the journal is newer than most adopters and Coherence received far more development attention than Mnemion during its life.

provenance.owner_words: the journal exists as COMPRESSION, not just memory. it is compression of possibly millions of subagent session tokens into a handful of durable, comprehensible outcomes. it is a signaling system so that subagents can compare notes. and it is a means of escalation for humans.

concepts.name: conjecture
concepts.definition: A side observation recorded while the cache is hot that would otherwise be lost: something that surprised the agent, what it could be, and the test that would separate the candidates. Not a decision; an open question a later agent may resolve or dismiss. The instrument-is-wrong candidate is always present.

rejected.because: a conjecture is an observation with no choice made; recording it as a decision would answer something nobody answered

provenance.purpose: Side observations and other reporting from expensive sessions are the highest-value compression the journal performs; a conjecture is how they survive.

concepts.name: defect
concepts.definition: A recorded behavioral deviation with the evidence that made it a defect: a user report about a UI bug, a field observation, or any deviation fuzzier than an invariant can record. Distinct from a structural defect, which is a state the tool derives for an invariant. Not every part of the car is structural steel.

rejected.alternative: fold into conjecture or into a requirement announcement
rejected.because: a defect is an assessed conclusion with evidence, not an open question, and it may never map to an invariant

provenance.owner_words: Defect can be a report from a user about a UI bug, or any other behavioral deviation which may be fuzzier than what an invariant can record. we cannot make the entire car out of structural steel.

properties.class: A defect's class: a short kebab-case name for the shape of the failure, shared by every defect of that shape, so one guard can cover them all. A class is declared once, as the property class <name> of defect, in Coherence's lexicon or the project's own; the defect verb refuses one declared nowhere.
properties.introduced: Where a defect came in: a commit, a pull request (PR #n), pre-existing (there before the work that found it), or unknown. A commit or pull request makes it fix-induced. A defect that never says is unknown, never guessed.
properties.caught: What caught a defect: review, ci, probe, adopter, self (the session that made it) or test.
properties.fix-induced: A defect whose introduced names a commit or a pull request: the work that was meant to fix or build something brought it in.
properties.guard: The invariant a defect's close names, as <component folder>/<name>, to protect the defect's whole class; it counts once its refutation is witnessed. A close names a guard or a decision saying why fixing the instance suffices; spec --check names a close with neither.
properties.guard failure: A defect recorded in a class a close had already guarded, after that close: the protection was weaker than claimed. spec --check and orient name it; the convergence reading counts it as a repeat of its class, which should fall to zero.
properties.escape: A defect whose introduced points into a release's range and that was recorded after the release's tag: it shipped.
properties.convergence: The reading of whether discoveries repay, over a window: defects arriving by origin and catch, escapes per release, the share closed with a guard, repeats per class, bullets over time, hotspot churn, and hook latency per Coherence version (query convergence).
properties.class path-identity: One file or folder spelled two ways (through a symbolic link, against another base, from the repository top instead of the project root) compares as two.
properties.class cost: Work out of proportion to the answer: a hook or reading that reads far more than it needs, past the latency budget.
properties.class ownership: One party's thing treated as another's: Coherence's lexicon, practice or decision demanded of or read as an adopter's, or the reverse.
properties.class structure-drift: What a spec, the lexicon or a document says has drifted from what the code or the files do, and no check sees it.
properties.class bypassed-door: A reference reaches a protected thing outside its chokepoint.
properties.class parse-gap: A reader of source, shell or spec text misses a shape its language allows.
properties.class root-resolution: The tool settled on the wrong project root, so it read, wrote or answered for the wrong tree.
properties.class overmatch: A pattern or check matches more than it means, so an unrelated thing satisfies or triggers it.
properties.class self-clearing: A check the very record or edit it guards can clear on its own.
properties.class exposure: Private state written where it is published or committed.
properties.class uninterpolated: Template text reaches a reader literally instead of the value it stands for.
properties.class load-flake: A test that fails under machine load whatever the change under test.
properties.class duplicated-fact: One fact kept in two places written apart, so one copy drifts from the other and a reader takes the stale one.
properties.class over-claim: A reading credits more than its evidence shows: a control, a coverage or a verification counted where nothing checks it, so a gap reads closed.
properties.class hand-built-path: A file of an installed package located by a path spelled by hand (a node_modules folder joined to a root) instead of asked of the package resolver, so a package manager that lays its packages out otherwise (pnpm's store, a package's exports) leaves it naming nothing.
properties.class version-skew: The Coherence that runs is not the one the adopter installed or meant: another copy shadows it, or a package manager resolved an older release than the project needs, and nothing says which version answers.
properties.class missing-entry-point: A way of reaching the tool that users expect is absent or answers wrongly: a conventional flag or verb (--version, --help) that is not recognized or is taken by the program in front of it.
properties.class false-alarm: A check reports a problem on input that is valid, such as a config, spec or lexicon an adopter wrote correctly or an earlier release wrote for it, so it fails CI or refuses a stop for nothing; guarded by the upgrade fixture carrying what adopters write.
properties.class merge-collision: Two branches' ordinary writes to a store Coherence commits conflict when the branches are merged or rebased, so people resolve by hand what git could have merged; guarded by the stack test that merges two branches' appends to every committed store.
properties.family audience: A reader is told the wrong thing for that reader, or not told what it needs: a message naming the wrong subject, guidance missing from what ships or from a practice. A family: too broad for one guard, so each defect closes with its own guard or a decision, and a later one is no guard failure.
properties.family hand-list: A list kept by hand that must mirror something defined elsewhere (files, imports, events, tools, keys), so the two drift and nothing fails: a module, an event or a tool silently left out. A family: each list is removed by deriving it from what it mirrors, one guard per list.
properties.family silent-skip: A reading, walk or command leaves part of what it was given out and says nothing about it. A family: every reader and command can skip in its own way, so each defect closes with its own guard or a decision, and a later one is no guard failure.
properties.mirror reading: The reading that finds hand lists: literal collections of names matched by overlap against each other and against what code derives (a folder's files, the import closure of a list of files, a module's exports, the keys a file reads), from git objects at one revision, with history naming the commit that grew one side alone (query mirrors). Advisory and never taken in a hook: orient names the groups worth a look from the last reading kept, and the reading proposes pairs for the edit-time alarm to watch.

concepts.name: experiment
concepts.definition: A plan made falsifiable before acting: predicted context, actions, and observable success criteria, closed by evidence for every criterion. The agent catches its own premature success instead of the human spending time detecting it. That is compression of the human's review, and a high success rate is evidence the mechanism works.

rejected.alternative: fold into decide with the prediction as the because
rejected.because: the value is the prediction being frozen before action and the close being derived from evidence per criterion; a decision records neither

provenance.owner_words: Experiment succeeding most of the time is evidence of the mechanism working correctly. it remains compression: instead of me spending time detecting premature success, the agent catches itself.

concepts.name: work order
concepts.definition: A named unit of assigned work, held by an owner session and moved through states. It carries an objective, an observable success criterion, a boundary and write scope, and the owner session set at creation; its states are open, active, waiting, completed and cancelled. Journal records and verification runs written by the owner session bind to it by inference. It grants no authority and gates nothing; its value is context, so a reader can see everything one assignment produced and why. Its create, moves and close may cite earlier records, and its reading lists what it cites, what binds to it, and what cites it.

rejected.alternative: authority model (granted-by, authority level, owner token expiring on handoff, orchestrator-only creation)
rejected.because: described in the hook, never enforced in code, routed around by every subagent; the substantive part of an order is its content
no consumer anywhere

concepts.name: unable
concepts.definition: A journal verb: this agent, in this session, could not get past a wall, and names the wall. A one-time password it does not hold, a runtime that ships no reporter, a history it cannot merge. It claims nothing about whether a human could; the reader decides that. Narrower than the reference verb it replaces.

The latest verdict per invariant is a view derived from runs, never stored as its own truth; a skipped enforcement keeps its prior dated verdict in the view.

properties.structure: The Structure view projects declared trust levels and crossing-bearing invariants in a stable order. Positions are computed from the current model, not maintained as separate layout truth.
properties.proposed_crossing: A proposed crossing is visibly provisional and carries no invented grade, verdict, bypass result or reliance evidence.
properties.live: A fixed shell whose bytes depend on no project content loads the state from the root's warm server, on loopback behind the root's token, and follows the journal, runs, work orders and specs as they change; a snapshot is the same shell with one state inline, for sharing and CI. The first load is a bounded window; older records load on demand by cursor.

concepts.name: agent query
concepts.definition: CLI access for the agent to what Scope shows a human. It is a small fixed set of questions with plain-text answers: which invariants touch these files, who relies on this chokepoint, what must be loaded to change this safely (the economy prediction), and what does my work order say. Fixed questions first; a query language only if the fixed set proves insufficient.

rejected.alternative: a general query language over the model
rejected.because: a second grammar to teach; fixed questions have known answer shapes an agent can act on
a former name for this concept in the reference implementation; refused so it cannot return as a second spelling

concepts.name: economy
concepts.definition: The context closure of a change: what a reader must load to modify one thing safely. The direct cost of a cold cache, predicted from the model (references, invariants, components).

concepts.name: calibrate
concepts.definition: Compares the economy prediction with what agents actually read in sessions, against labeled outcomes, so the prediction can be corrected. Read traces are its input.

concepts.name: mass
concepts.definition: A diagnostic reporting two numbers side by side for each component and the project: total mass and unreached mass. Total mass counts lines, files and symbols; unreached mass is code in no component, or in a component that no invariant's chokepoint or oracle references. A large object with no definition is an unbalanced, wobbly load the agent should instinctively be cautious with.

rejected.alternative: mass as a ratchet pinned to a baseline that fails on growth
rejected.because: growth is not the danger; weight with no definition is. The way down is an invariant, not a deletion.
a former name for this concept in the reference implementation; refused so it cannot return as a second spelling

provenance.metaphor: Coherence is a prosthetic for proprioception. Mass is the felt weight of a part of the project; unreached mass is weight with nothing holding it.

concepts.name: gyroscope
concepts.definition: The lifecycle as a whole: the mechanism that provides proprioceptive balance to an agent session. Two readings of one model at two moments of the cycle: orient at the start, regulate at the end.

provenance.owner_words: the goal here for lifecycle is the gyroscope that provides the proprioceptive balance. orient should be at the start of the cycle, regulate should supply the balance for the end of that cycle.

concepts.name: orient
concepts.definition: The start-of-cycle reading. Before acting, the session sees where the project stands and what heading follows from it. It shows escalations awaiting a human, structural defects, requirements stuck short of invariant, unreached mass, the session's own work order, and what peers recorded. One heading, derived from state; it also names the spec gaps beyond the adoption baseline.

rejected.alternative: orient and regulate as two competing machines over the same ledgers
rejected.because: they are one model read at two moments

concepts.name: regulate
concepts.definition: The end-of-cycle reading: what the session owes at its stop, to leave the project no less coherent than it found it. Candidates: an invariant touched without a run, a requirement declared without its checklist, a structural defect revealed and not acknowledged or repaired, a decision made and not recorded, and, advisory, a spec gap the session touched.

concepts.name: config
concepts.definition: The list of project facts the tool cannot derive. They are: name, entry dir, ignore patterns, language, how to run tests and match their names, where tests live, the well-known names the project vouches for (wellKnown), and the interface reading's budget (interfaceBudget). Every key that configures a mechanism leaves with the mechanism.

properties.test setup: One runner's way of running tests: its commands, the test files it claims (by language or file globs), and the folder it starts in. The single test keys are one setup; the tests key lists several, for a project whose languages run under different runners.
properties.languages: A project may list more than one language; each file's language is its extension, the first listed is the primary, and each language has its own warm server.
properties.registry: A config at a repository top that lists projects: the folders opted in, each a project inheriting the registry keys its own config does not set, and the top no project of its own. A config the registry does not list is a problem, never half adopted.

concepts.name: scaffold
concepts.definition: The command that makes the complete shape the cheapest thing to ship. Two shapes: a component (folder plus spec with intent and empty invariants) and an invariant (bullet with slots for enforcement, because, crossing, the entrances it covers, refutation, and the decomposition checklist printed beside it as declare-or-dismiss lines). The agent fills slots instead of recalling rules. For a spec gap it proposes the closure in those same terms: an entrances: line naming the entrance on a verified invariant that covered it by its crossing alone, a guard: line, an invariant bullet whose crossing enters from the entrance's trust and whose entrances: line names it, or control: none with a reason. Scope shows a visual preview of the proposed structure before it is written, so a human can see the new vertebra in place.

rejected.because: one grammar leaves two shapes

properties.preview: A derived reading of an intended change before the spec is written. Creating that reading does not apply the spec change or verify the invariant; writing requires the explicit write action.

concepts.name: peer feed
concepts.definition: The simpler signaling channel for subagents. Before each tool use, the hook injects the subjects of decisions peers have recorded since the last injection, not their full text. Delta-tracked per session. An agent that wants the full record reads the journal.

rejected.alternative: full records with previews, truncation, escaped fragments, and a pending queue at every boundary

kinds.rule: Two kinds, and no other. Decisions are what this concept was defined for. Escalations ride with them because an escalation heads every read: a question standing before a human changes what a peer should do next, and a session that learns of one only at its own start would act past it for a whole cycle. Every other verb stays in the journal, one command away, where a reader who wants it goes. Decided 2026-09-18 with the lexicon in view; the owner may narrow it back to decisions alone.
kinds.open: A retraction of a decision a peer may already have acted on is the strongest candidate for a third kind; it was left out because the feed carries subjects and a retraction's subject is an id, which reads as noise until the reader fetches the record anyway.

concepts.name: lexicon
concepts.definition: A required component of every Coherence project: lexicon.json, the settled vocabulary with, for each concept, its definition, its aliases, and the names rejected for it and why. Injected into context the way a project's standing instructions to agents are; no run can miss it.

properties.anti_rot: The lexicon names things and never points at where they live in code. No addresses, so a rename or move cannot stale it.
properties.anti_fragile: Every attempt to introduce a name makes the lexicon stronger: a new noun in a spec, journal entry, or identifier is caught at regulate and must be declared as a new concept, mapped as an alias, or fixed if it is a rejected name. Rejected names accumulate as the record of what drift was refused.
properties.two_layers: Coherence's own lexicon (the tool vocabulary) and each project's domain lexicon share one shape and one mechanism; scaffold for a new project begins by asking for the domain lexicon.
properties.growth: Asymmetric, like invariants: agents propose and announce new concepts; only a human retires or renames one. Each definition change is a decision with a rejected alternative.
properties.injection: Compact: name, one-line definition, rejected names. Full entries through agent query.
properties.naming_check: Identifiers are checked against rejected names and misused concept names by word, not by address.
properties.baseline: What was already here when work began, remembered so only what is new speaks. In an adopter, the findings its lexicon check held at adoption, recorded as a journal decision (lexicon baseline) the check then fails only beyond; every later baseline record is intersected with the earlier ones, so it only shrinks. For a session, the vocabulary uses observed at its start. Coherence's own repository keeps no lexicon check baseline: its text is enforced whole.
properties.where_rejected_names_bind: Coherence's rejected names bind only where Coherence's concepts are named: everywhere in Coherence's own repository; in an adopter, only in the text written to Coherence (records, spec grammar, coherence.config.json), and there as advisory. A project's own rejected names bind in all of its text, and a word the project declares in its own lexicon is its own inside it.

rejected.alternative: concept addressing (each concept lists where it is implemented in code)
rejected.because: invites drift; an address is a claim about code that rots when the code moves
Owner ruled 2026-09-23 (d-cb376a86): glossary reads as a passive appendix, while the thing settles, rejects and is enforced; lexicon names the project's own words without the appendix connotation

detail.similarity_seam: The drift check matches exact strings first (new noun, rejected name). A similarity seam is left open so an embedding pass can later suggest candidate mappings for near-synonyms and flag overloads by clustering the contexts of a term across components. Similarity only improves the closed question (declare, map, or fix); it never decides. Planned as a local service: the supported platform is Apple Silicon only, so an on-device model needs no API key and no network. Backend under survey 2026-09-17.
detail.first_class: Coherence needs first-class support for building, maintaining, and validating the lexicon. Building: draft from specs, docs, component names, and tool surface; settle collisions by ruling. Maintaining: the vocabulary check at regulate; only a human retires or renames. Validating: sense, not names; a periodic per-concept review the tool makes cheap, approximated mechanically by the similarity seam. See docs/lexicon.md.

provenance.owner_words: glossary.json. Injected into context same as AGENTS.md. no run can miss it. glossary must be anti-rot, anti-fragile. Coherence will need first class support for building, maintaining and validating the glossary.

concepts.name: agent host
concepts.definition: The application that runs an agent session and supplies its lifecycle events and tool results. Coherence delivers readings through hooks in that application.

concepts.name: structure
concepts.definition: The reading of what a system is made of and how work flows through it. It lets a human inspect and reason about the behavior of a system agentic coding has made opaque, and extends to a change set as a visual diff of how the change affects structure and behavior.

provenance.owner_words: Arrows point the way work goes, caller to callee, yes. Zoom makes sense. Diff compared to previous commit, or to a specific commit the agent provides for the user. Stable positions are essential and that rule makes sense. One map, yes. Seven is a good start. We'll test and revisit.

detail.evidence_tier: Structure states the tier of its evidence on screen. Static and computed (resolved references, declared entrances, invariants) is the default. Observed runtime behavior is a separate, labeled tier, never blended in unlabeled.
detail.direction: Arrows point the way work goes: caller to callee. Data paths are a highlight on selecting a trust level, never a second arrow.
detail.zoom: One level of the component tree at a time, expanding in place; a collapsed component shows its heaviest component interfaces at its edge; code in no component is shown as its own labeled mass.
detail.diff: A change set is compared with the previous commit by default, or with a commit the agent names for the user. Measures: entrance added or removed; component interface added, removed, or widened (references new symbols); chokepoint gaining a bypass; crossing added or removed; data path gaining a branch.
detail.stability: Positions are never stored and must be stable: layout is a pure function of entrances and component interfaces with ties broken by name, and a change that adds one component interface moves only the components it touches.
detail.one_map: One map. The security spine is selecting a trust level; reliance is selecting a component interface's chokepoint. No separate spine section and no separate reliance view.
detail.success: Each reviewer question is answerable from the map in one selection: where does work enter; what does this change touch; where does sensitive data go; what is load-bearing here; what did this change weaken. To be tested and revisited.

concepts.name: entrance
concepts.definition: Where work enters the system from outside it: a command, a host event, a route, a tool. Declared in the owning component's spec and checked against the code: the named handler (a symbol, or a module file whose top-level script receives the work) must resolve and be reachable, so a declared entrance cannot rot unseen. It declares the trust level it carries in with a trust: line; without one, its trust is derived from the crossings on its handler. A guard: line names the chokepoint its handler is registered through, counted once the reading confirms the registration. A control: none line with its reason says it needs no control: a stated claim Scope shows for a human to challenge, never beside a guard:.

provenance.owner_words: Declared and checked for entrypoints is good.

properties.entrance coverage: How much of the surface the reading detects the declared entrances cover: each detected entrance is covered individually (an entrance's handler names it and nothing else), through a grouped entrance (one entrance stands for every detected entrance registered through its handler or detected in its module), or undeclared. A spec-gap count speaks only for the covered part.
properties.detected entrance: An entrance the reading finds by one of the rules its language lists (a server function, a server route, a URL pattern, a package script, a top-level script), with the rule and why it matched; never a guess presented as fact.

concepts.name: component interface
concepts.definition: The surface one component exposes and another uses. Computed, never declared, as the set of resolved references from one component to another, so Structure is a live view of the real project, not a rotting map. What it reveals comes from the invariants: its chokepoint if one stands there, its crossing if trust changes there, and the classes of data that pass through it.

provenance.owner_words: Interface is good. Computed is essential, we need this to be a live view of the real project, not a rotting map. / component interface as qualification?

concepts.name: observation
concepts.definition: A record of runtime behavior from a named source, bound to a commit and a session. The source is a test pass, later a trace window; an observation is never read as current once its commit is not the head.

detail.staleness: An observation whose commit is not the head, or whose tree was dirty when it was captured, is stale and every reader says so; it is never blended into the current reading unlabeled.
detail.co-execution: Coverage records what executed, not who called whom: a component interface is crossed in a test when a referencing site in one component and the referenced symbol's body in the other both executed in that test. The record says co-executed, never called.
detail.attribution: Per test where the runner can attribute coverage to a test; per run, said so, where it cannot. Per-test attribution is never fabricated.

provenance.owner_words: do it (runtime overlay on Structure)

concepts.name: structural route
concepts.definition: The path one entrance takes through the components it reaches, in the order work flows, as one line of its own color. Computed from the entrance and the component interfaces, never declared. Components on more than one structural route are where those routes meet; entrances share one only when they share its stops, its trust, and what they declare of their control. Its controls are traced, never declared: the interface identifiers on its lines, and the verified chokepoints wrapping its handler or standing inside a component on it, and verified totality oracles on it covering its trust. An untrusted route with none is marked no traced control, which is not a demonstrated bypass, unless its entrances declare control: none, which it shows as no control needed.

provenance.owner_words: structural route. not utility, core dependency. not tag. interface identifier

concepts.name: core dependency
concepts.definition: A component that most other components call. Structure draws it as a rail its callers attach to by a short stub rather than as an arrow from every caller. Computed from the component interfaces, never declared.

provenance.owner_words: not utility, core dependency

concepts.name: interface identifier
concepts.definition: The short identifier drawn on a component interface where a chokepoint or a crossing stands, like a valve tag on a pipe. The map shows only the identifier; its meaning is in the inspector. Never truncated, and dropped by priority rather than overlapped.

provenance.owner_words: not tag. interface identifier

concepts.name: well-known name
concepts.definition: A name with so much gravity in training data that no project definition could make it less ambiguous. It is the proper name of a widely used technology, language, platform, vendor, standard, or format (Python, Pyright, GitHub), a name a project vouches for in its config, or the project's own name. A well-known name is never a vocabulary candidate. A common word a project gives its own sense (hive, scope, core, run, session) is never one, even written as a proper noun; a name whose lowercase is an ordinary word (Node, Chrome) is well known only in its capitalized spelling.

properties.curated_list: Shipped with the tool beside vocabulary coverage, versioned, with its rule for inclusion written at its top.
properties.capitalized_only: A name whose lowercase spelling is an ordinary word is well known only in its capitalized spelling; its lowercase use in a project sense stays a candidate.
properties.not_entries: A name a concept lists as not to be confused with is already known to the lexicon and is not listed again.

provenance.defined_by: agent proposal during the vocabulary coverage redesign, 2026-09-23 (journal d-c8f34e4b)
provenance.because: The owner ruled that names with so much gravity there is no fear of ambiguity need no definition, while a common word in a project sense still does.

concepts.name: citation
concepts.definition: A record's checked pointer to an earlier record it rests on or is about. It names the record by id, in either store and of any kind; it is given with --cite on decisions, conjectures, defects, experiments, unable, escalations, and work order creates, moves and closes, and an id that names no record refuses the write. Untyped, and read both ways: what a record cites, and what cites it, derived at every read.

rejected.alternative: typed citations naming what one record does to another (implements, repairs, verifies, authorizes)
rejected.because: the work order's typed consequences were written by the closing session restating its own close and never read back; a reader needs to know that one record rests on another, and the record's own text says how

rejected.alternative: a record id written into a because as plain text
rejected.because: never resolved or checked; a typo or an id from another checkout reads as a relationship to nothing, and no reader can walk it back

rejected.alternative: a citedBy field written onto the cited record
rejected.because: the stores are append only; the reverse direction is derived at read time, so an old record gains its citers without an edit

detail.validation: Every cited id must name a record already in the journal or the work store when the citation is written; one unknown id refuses the whole write and appends nothing. An id given twice is refused. A record that cites nothing carries no cites field, so records written before citations read unchanged.
detail.reading: journal and journal --json show each record's cites and what cites it; journal <id> names both directions by kind and subject; work inspect and query order list what an order's records cite, what binds to it, and what cites it; Scope's Journal view links both directions; orient names what an open escalation cites. The peer feed stays subjects only.
detail.scope_window: Scope's first load keeps, one hop and up to a cap, the older records its kept records and work orders cite; a citation past the cap shows its id, which the live page loads on request and a snapshot answers with the command that reads it.

provenance.defined_by: agent relations (session a40acfaebbf15f7f7), 2026-09-23, on the owner-approved approach for relationships between journal and work records

concepts.name: spec gap
concepts.definition: An untrusted entrance with no traced control. Its trust is a level from outside the system's control, or unknown, no control is traced on its structural route, and it declares no control: none. It closes three ways: a guard: line, an invariant whose crossing enters from its trust and whose entrances: line names it, or control: none with a reason. Orient names the gaps beyond the adoption baseline, and how many lost a control an invariant gave by its crossing alone; regulate names the ones a session touched; neither is a demonstrated bypass.

provenance.owner_words: let's do 1-3, and then test the results on a pre-Coherence commit from both of those projects to see if the behavior change is effective

concepts.name: hook voice
concepts.definition: A project's own text at a hook event, in place of or after what the hook says. The override file, .coherence/hooks/<Event>.override.md, replaces the event's canonical text (an empty one is a deliberate silence), and the append file, .coherence/hooks/<Event>.append.md, follows it; a refusal's reason is never replaced.

provenance.defined_by: agent hook-voice (session c1db1b63-f5b7-4dc3-94a8-3c324ee41fcb), 2026-09-28 (journal d-9a9d08cb), restoring the reference per-event override and append files (fb445b2)
provenance.owner_words: yeah, have a subagent restore hook overrides and addenda

concepts.definition: A component's recorded method for a kind of work, kept in the practice file paired with its spec. A spec and a practice file are always paired: no practice file stands without a sister spec, and project-wide practices sit beside the entry spec. Each practice is one bullet in the spec grammar naming its trigger (when), ordered steps with the evidence each leaves, pitfalls citing the records that witnessed them, the records it was learned from, and its because; an invariant named in a step resolves against the sister spec. Adding a step or a pitfall is free; removing one needs a cited record. A practice is a candidate until its first enactment in which every step that names its evidence produced it; then it is established. The hook delivers a practice when its trigger fires.

rejected.alternative: process as the name of this concept
rejected.because: pulls toward the operating-system sense, which the tool's own text and code already use (subprocess, process tree)

rejected.alternative: a practices section inside the spec
rejected.because: a spec says what must hold and a practice says how work is done; a sister file gives the practice its own history, its own check rules, and a load the hook can make without parsing invariants

rejected.alternative: practice files in folders without a spec
rejected.because: pairing keeps the component the unit, so a folder never becomes half a component

concepts.name: practice

properties.trigger: What fires a practice, on its when: line: a command's words, an edited path's glob with the text the edit adds, or explicit. The hook reads it before the tool runs.
properties.step: One thing the practice says to do, numbered from one in the order written; an enactment gives every step an outcome.
properties.leaves: The evidence a step leaves behind, named under it: a run record, a journal record, a file state. A step that names one is auditable; one that does not is taken at its word.
properties.pitfall: A way the practice has failed, citing the record or commit that witnessed it. Delivered with the practice, after its steps.
properties.learned: The records and commits the practice was learned from. A practice that cites nothing is a problem: it is learned, not wished.
properties.version: A fingerprint of the triggers, steps and pitfalls; an enactment binds to the version it carried out.
properties.reach: How far one of Coherence's own practices goes, on its reach: line: kernel (every adopter receives it) or internal (it never leaves Coherence's tree). Required in Coherence's tree, refused elsewhere.

concepts.definition: The journal record that a session carried out a practice: the practice, the version enacted, what triggered it, and a result for each step. A practice is enacted. Each step is done, with its evidence where the step names one, or deviated or skipped, each with a because. A deviation is how a practice improves; a step left out silently is how it decays. Enactments are what the practice's integrity is read from: a step removed without a cited record, a step claimed done whose evidence is missing, and a trigger with no enactment by stop.

concepts.name: enactment

concepts.definition: A practice Coherence ships that every adopter receives beside its own. In Coherence's own tree each practice declares its reach: reach: kernel ships it to every adopter, where its id is led by coherence: and its steps arrive when its trigger fires; reach: internal keeps it in Coherence's tree, an internal practice, because its steps are about Coherence itself. The reach is a value set rather than yes or no, so a later reach is one more value. A project's own practices carry no reach.

latency budget
concepts.definition: The most seconds a tool hook may take, counted from its process's start: 3 unless the config declares latencyBudget. A tool hook (PreToolUse, PostToolUse) runs around every tool call, so its time is paid over and over, and a call cycle that feels sluggish gets Coherence switched off, which loses every check at once. A tool hook over it names its own time in its answer; regulate names the session's calls over it with what the tool hooks cost in all, and orient the last week's. A count of work (an execution-budget invariant: git spawns per question, per tool call) guards the known shapes; the latency budget is the measured time, and alarms on what no count names. Not the budget checklist kind, whose shapes bound one operation's admission, memory and steps.

concepts.name: CI check
concepts.definition: Coherence run on every pull request by the project's CI host. It runs spec --check and the chokepoint run in one of two modes the user chooses: fail, where the check fails on a spec problem or a structural defect, or comment, where one report comment on the pull request carries the findings and the check fails only when Coherence itself breaks. ci install writes its workflow; ci report builds the comment.

concepts.name: quint model
concepts.definition: The .qnt model a spec names on its model: line. It writes the component's behavior as guarded actions over pure updates, which a quint prop checks and conformance replay holds against the code; a spec with no model says none or planned, with the reason, on the same line.

concepts.name: quint prop
concepts.definition: A totality oracle whose detector is quint. Its via: reads quint prop <property>, a property of the spec's quint model, checked by quint typecheck, quint run and quint verify, and graded verified or simulated; it never passes on a step that did not answer.

concepts.name: conformance replay
concepts.definition: The code's own tests replayed through its quint model. Each instrumented site logs an event to a collector while the tests run, and every captured trace replays through the model with arguments pinned by name and conformance facts guarding the state it computes; green only when every trace replays and coverage holds.

concepts.name: conformance fact
concepts.definition: A logged post-state fact a model action guards on. The code logs it after a mutation as an extra argument named as the action's parameter, and the action guards it equal to its own computed post-state, so a replay that disagrees fails the guard; opt in per operation, and only as strong as the fact chosen.

concepts.name: collector
concepts.definition: The loopback server the tests post events to. The conform command starts it before the tests; it takes one scoped event per POST /test/<name>, queues a test's trace when its outcome is ok, discards it when failed, and refuses a client that speaks another protocol version.

concepts.name: landmark
concepts.definition: A model boolean naming a moment worth reaching. It is written val landmark_<name> in a quint model; a behavior family is the ordered sequence in which a trace's landmarks first fire, and every landmark must be reached by some test.

concepts.name: behavior family
concepts.definition: The order in which a trace's landmarks first fire. The same landmarks in another order, [b, a] against [a, b], are a different family, so whether a test covered a behavior is decidable; a family the model can reach and no test covers is blind.

concepts.name: guard scenario
concepts.definition: One guard conjunct of one model action. Replay records whether a step found it true and found it false; one that can be false and never was is a gap, and one no input can falsify must be widened or acknowledged with a reason.

metaphors.spine: Invariants are the spine; removing a vertebra changes the shape and integrity of the system.
metaphors.automobile: Most projects need a structure closer to an automobile than an octopus; detailed invariants keep load-bearing members from being opaquely weakened.
metaphors.proprioception: Coherence is a prosthetic for proprioception: the agent should feel the weight and balance of what it is moving. Unreached mass is a wobbly load.
metaphors.structural_steel: Not every part of the car is structural steel; defects can be fuzzier than an invariant records.
